subject: Post-demo: model shortlist & recommended evals
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan@acme.com>, Priya Singh <priya@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + recommended model shortlist

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the thoughtful questions. Quick recap and the model shortlist we recommend for Acme's RAG-powered customer assistant use case (quality, latency, cost tradeoffs included). Attaching the detailed benchmark CSV and a prompt set we suggest for evaluation.

Top recommended models (priority order):
1) Llama 3 70B (8k context) - high quality / best for complex instruction-following and multi-turn context. Expect ~200-350 ms token latency on our dedicated 1xA100 profile; higher token cost but best for minimizing hallucination on long contexts.
2) Mistral-Instruct-7B (8k) - strong quality-to-cost tradeoff; much lower inference cost and median token latency ~80-120 ms, good for high throughput flows.
3) Redstone-13B-quant (q4f16) - quantized variant optimized for latency/cost; slightly lower top-end quality but very cheap per-token, useful for lower-risk fallbacks and bulk tasks.

Notes on evaluation focus:
- We recommend running your top 200 prompt examples (attached prompt-set-v1.jsonl) across models to measure intent extraction, factuality on product data, and hallucination rate.
- We flagged two prompt families that historically expose regressions: long-document summarization and policy interpretation prompts. Please include them in the eval slices.
- See attached benchmark-results.csv for our synthetic latency/cost numbers on similar RAG workloads.

Next steps (proposed):
- You upload a redacted sample of your prompt/test set or confirm we should use the attached prompt-set as-is.
- We provision eval tokens and a sandbox endpoint (48–72 hrs) for you to run the tests, or we can run an initial pass and return metrics.
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up after the eval to review tradeoffs and recommended config (batching, prefix cache settings, quantization profile).

Attachments: acme-model-shortlist.pdf, benchmark-results.csv, prompt-set-v1.jsonl

Thanks — happy to adjust the shortlist if you have additional constraints (on-device latency targets, price cap, or regulatory data residency).

Best,
Marissa Cole

Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + recommended model shortlist

Love this summary — a couple of practical numbers for budgeting and config:
- For the Llama 3 70B profile we recommended, plan for roughly $0.45–0.60 per 1k tokens on hosted, or ~35% lower unit cost on Dedicated with a 3-month commit.
- Mistral-7B typically winds up ~4x cheaper per-token with slightly higher error on long context Q&A slices.
- For RAG, enable prefix KV caching and moderate batching (batch_size=8–16) to get stable latency while saving 20–30% on token compute.

Quality/regression note: when we move between model families (e.g., 70B -> 13B quant), watch the hallucination precision on product recall prompts — we recommend running the "recall_accuracy" slice from the prompt set immediately. Happy to own the first eval run if you want us to.

—Rishi
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + recommended model shortlist

Thanks, Marissa — this is really helpful. A few clarifying Qs:
1) For our primary use (RAG + short customer replies), which two models would you prioritize for a quick A/B (we want to minimize latency for peak traffic but cannot compromise on product recall)?
2) Can you confirm the setup you recommend for the sandbox endpoints (CPU/GPU profile, max tokens, streaming enabled)?
3) We'll upload 250 redacted prompts — where should we put them? Is the Drive link secure for PII?

If you can provision the sandbox + eval tokens and run the first pass on our prompt set (especially the recall_accuracy slice), that would be ideal — we can iterate from the results. Also, what's the expected turnaround for the eval run?

Jordan

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + recommended model shortlist

Great questions — answers below and next steps.

1) Priority A/B: start with Llama 3 70B (baseline high-quality) vs Mistral-Instruct-7B (cost/latency winner). Those two give a clear picture of high-quality vs efficient tradeoffs for RAG. If the recall_accuracy delta is too large, we'll test Redstone-13B-quant as a fallback.

2) Sandbox config we will provision: 1xA100 (or equivalent) GPU profile with streaming enabled, max response_tokens=1024 for the tests, and default prefix KV cache on. We'll also provide a Mistral-7B profile on a smaller GPU for latency comparison. If you prefer Dedicated-like throughput, we can mirror a 2xA100 reserved config (estimating 30% lower per-token latency at higher commit cost).

3) Upload: use the secure Drive link below (works with our internal DLP and is scoped to the account you provide). If you need encrypted upload, we can provide an S3 presigned with KMS envelope.

Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/acme/prompt-set-v1
Eval turnaround: if you provide the 250 prompts by EOD tomorrow, we can run the first pass within 48 hours and deliver a short evaluation report (recall_accuracy, hallucination rate, latency percentiles).

I've attached the short model shortlist PDF and the CSV with our benchmark numbers. I'll provision the sandbox and drop credentials into the Drive folder once the prompts arrive. Also attaching a DocuSign link for the MSA (optional at evaluation stage) if you prefer to lock in commit pricing earlier: https://docusign.net/Redwood/ACME-MSA

Next-step checklist:
- Jordan: upload prompts to the Drive link (or say if you want S3 KMS).
- Redwood: provision sandbox + eval tokens (I'll confirm by email when ready).
- Schedule 30-min follow-up: how's Tue 3/23 10am PT?

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call to walk the team through the prompt slice definitions so the eval focuses on your top risk areas.

Best,
